news.title: U-17 World Cup: Flamingos urged to maintain momentum against North Korea
news.lede: Football fans have praised Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, the Flamingos, following their 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico at the ongoing FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, urging the players to sustain their momentum in their final group match against North Korea. The result has further strengthened Nigeria’s hopes of progressing to the knockout stage, with fans in Aba, Abia State, urging the team to remain focused and clinical in front of goal against their highly rated opponents. Read Also: Flamingos beat Puerto Rico 2-0 to boost U-17 World Cup hopes. Amarachi Amaechi, a football enthusiast, urged the Flamingos to approach the decisive encounter with determination, warning against being intimidated by North Korea’s impressive scoring record.

news.title: Turkiye replace coach after poor results in Nations League, World Cup
news.lede: Former Turkiye international and Besiktas coach has been brought in to replace Vincenzo Montella in the Crescent Stars hot seat. Türkiye have appointed Sergen Yalcin as new coach, the Türkiye Football Federation (TFF) announced on Tuesday. The former Turkiye midfielder, 53, replaces Vincenzo Montella, who recently departed the role following a series of poor results in the recent international window. Turkiye lost all four of their UEFA Nations League games, including two defeats to Italy plus a 1-0 loss to France and 3-0 reverse in Belgium.

news.title: Oman U15s land in Baku for historic Fifa World Cup campaign
news.lede: MUSCAT: Oman’s under-15 national football team arrived in Azerbaijan on Wednesday ahead of its historic participation in the inaugural Fifa U15 World Cup and Festival 2026, marking an important milestone in the Sultanate of Oman’s youth football development programme. The delegation travelled to Baku following an intensive domestic camp in Muscat, during which the technical staff focused on raising the players’ physical readiness, sharpening tactical discipline and helping the youngsters adapt to the demands of international competition. Led by national head coach Nasser al Mayahi, Oman have been drawn in Group B alongside Argentina, Algeria, Malawi, Chinese Taipei and Suriname. The Young Reds will begin their campaign against Suriname on October 24 before facing Malawi and Argentina on October 25.
